## ChipProps

```typescript
interface ChipProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>
```

A tag the reader can scan past.

Bordered, pill-shaped, muted, `--text-sm`. Use it for a filter, a
label, a piece of metadata — something that describes the row it
sits on.

`Chip` and `Badge` take the same props and are not
interchangeable. If the thing you are showing is a *state* that
changes — ready, failed, three unread — it is a `Badge`,
which is filled by tone and bold so it is noticed. If it is a fact
about the thing, it is a `Chip`.

| Member | Kind | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `tone` | field | `Tone` |

## Chip

```typescript
function Chip({ tone = "neutral", className, ...rest }: ChipProps)
```

**Also** [`ChipProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#chipprops).

## BadgeProps

```typescript
interface BadgeProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>
```

A state the reader is meant to notice.

Filled by tone, bold, `--text-xs`, no border. See `ChipProps`
for which of the two to reach for.

The tone is colour, and colour alone is not a message: put the
state in the text too. "Failed" in a danger badge survives being
read aloud and being looked at by somebody who cannot tell it from
the success one; an empty red badge does not.

| Member | Kind | Type |
|---|---|---|
| `tone` | field | `Tone` |

## Badge

```typescript
function Badge({ tone = "neutral", className, ...rest }: BadgeProps)
```

**Also** [`BadgeProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#badgeprops).

## EmptyProps

```typescript
interface EmptyProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>
```

What to show where there is nothing.

Its own component rather than a paragraph with a class, because an
empty state that says only "nothing here" is the commonest way a
panel wastes the one moment it had the reader's attention. The
`action` slot is a nudge to say what to do next.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | field | `ReactNode` | A button, usually: the one thing to do about being empty. |

## Empty

```typescript
function Empty({ children, action, className, ...rest }: EmptyProps)
```

**Also** [`EmptyProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#emptyprops).

## DialogProps

```typescript
interface DialogProps extends Omit<HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>, "title">
```

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | field | `ReactNode` |  |
| `sub` | field | `ReactNode` | Shown under the title. A sentence, not a paragraph. |
| `children` | field | `ReactNode` |  |
| `actions` | field | `ReactNode` | The buttons. Rendered in an `Actions` row at the foot. |
| `onClose` | field | `() => void` | Escape, or a click on the backdrop. |

## Dialog

```typescript
function Dialog({ title, sub, children, actions, onClose, className, ...rest }: DialogProps)
```

The one primitive here that is behaviour rather than a box.

A dialog has to trap focus, close on Escape, restore focus to
whatever opened it, and not let a click inside the panel count as a
click on the backdrop. Every extension that built its own would get
some of that wrong, and the ones they get wrong are the ones only
keyboard and screen-reader users notice.

**Also** [`DialogProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#dialogprops).

## Checkbox

```typescript
function Checkbox({ label, className, ...rest }: CheckboxProps)
```

A native checkbox, wrapped in its own label.

Wrapped rather than associated by `id`, because an `id` an
extension forgets to make unique is a label that checks somebody
else's box — and nothing about the page looks wrong when it does.

**Also** [`CheckboxProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#checkboxprops).

## SwitchProps

```typescript
interface SwitchProps extends Omit<ButtonHTMLAttributes<HTMLButtonElement>, "onChange">
```

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `checked` | field | `boolean` |  |
| `onChange` | field | `(next: boolean) => void` |  |
| `label` | field | `ReactNode` | Shown beside the switch, and used as its accessible name. |

## Switch

```typescript
function Switch({ checked, onChange, label, className, ...rest }: SwitchProps)
```

A switch, which is a button rather than a checkbox.

The difference is not cosmetic. A checkbox is a value you submit; a
switch takes effect the moment it moves. `role="switch"` is what
tells a screen reader which of those it is looking at.

**Also** [`SwitchProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#switchprops).

## FieldProps

```typescript
interface FieldProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>
```

A label, a control, and room for the reason it is wrong.

The error slot is the part that gets left out, and a form that
rejects input without saying why is the one people abandon. When
`error` is set it is wired to the control through
`aria-describedby`, so it is announced rather than merely shown.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | field | `ReactNode` |  |
| `hint` | field | `ReactNode` |  |
| `error` | field | `ReactNode` |  |
| `htmlFor` | field | `string` | The id of the control, so the label points at it. |

## Field

```typescript
function Field({ label, hint, error, htmlFor, children, className, ...rest }: FieldProps)
```

**Also** [`FieldProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#fieldprops).

## SpinnerProps

```typescript
interface SpinnerProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLSpanElement>
```

Work whose duration is unknown. `Skeleton` is for known shapes.

`label` is required for the same reason `Progress.label` is. This
was `role="status"` on an empty span: a live region with nothing
to say, so a screen reader got silence while a sighted user
watched something spin.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` | field | `string` | Required: a spinner with no name is a live region with nothing in it. |

## Spinner

```typescript
function Spinner({ label, className, ...rest }: SpinnerProps)
```

**Also** [`SpinnerProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#spinnerprops).

```typescript

```

Tabs with the arrow keys wired, because a tab strip that only
responds to clicks is a tab strip half the people cannot use.

**Also** [`TabsProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#tabsprops).

## TabPanelProps

```typescript
interface TabPanelProps extends HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>
```

The panel a tab controls. Needs the same `base` the strip used.

Published because `Tabs` without it is half the ARIA pattern: the
strip announced that it controlled something and there was nothing
for it to control.

| Member | Kind | Type | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `base` | field | `string` | The id prefix shared with its `Tabs`, so the two agree. |
| `id` | field | `string` | Which tab this panel belongs to. |
| `active` | field | `string` | Which tab is showing. The panel renders only when they match. |

## TabPanel

```typescript
function TabPanel({ base, id, active, children, className, ...rest }: TabPanelProps)
```

**Also** [`TabPanelProps`](/docs/sdk/ui-react/reference-the-primitives#tabpanelprops).
